acceptance_checks.given: the archived rescue is the implementation baseline
acceptance_checks.then: the archived rescue acceptance checks SHALL remain passing

acceptance_checks.given: a valid singleton Google configuration
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL persist exactly one immutable account ID for the legacy connection

acceptance_checks.given: the singleton migration has completed
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL produce no duplicate account, token, mapping, or event rewrite

acceptance_checks.given: a legacy token cannot be copied and verified
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL retain the legacy token slot and fail without partial activation

acceptance_checks.given: a configured account has tokens, mappings, cursors, and event targets
acceptance_checks.then: every immutable identity and storage key SHALL remain byte-for-byte unchanged

acceptance_checks.given: OAuth token material is persisted
acceptance_checks.when: a token storage address is resolved
acceptance_checks.then: every OAuth token SHALL be addressed by immutable account ID rather than alias or email

acceptance_checks.given: OAuth is pending for account A
acceptance_checks.when: a callback carries state bound to account B
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL reject the callback without persisting token material

acceptance_checks.given: a migrated token lacks CalendarList scope
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL preserve local data and mark only its account `needs_reauth`

acceptance_checks.given: Google returns visible calendars for a connected account
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL persist every returned calendar under that account ID

acceptance_checks.given: a calendar is discovered for the first time
acceptance_checks.when: its registry state is first persisted
acceptance_checks.then: its enabled state SHALL default to true

acceptance_checks.given: a disabled existing calendar and a newly visible calendar
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL preserve the existing disable while enabling the new calendar

acceptance_checks.given: a known calendar is absent from a later discovery response
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL mark it unavailable without deleting cached canonical events

acceptance_checks.given: an enabled reader or freeBusyReader calendar
acceptance_checks.when: agenda and destination capabilities are projected
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL mirror its events while excluding it from mutation destinations

acceptance_checks.given: a calendar with queued writes loses writer/owner access
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL pause those writes with `provider_permission_changed` without rerouting

acceptance_checks.given: a calendar is disabled or unavailable
acceptance_checks.then: sync SHALL issue no provider request for that destination

acceptance_checks.given: two accounts expose identical calendar IDs and Google event IDs
acceptance_checks.then: their cursor and mapping rows SHALL remain independently addressable

acceptance_checks.given: one destination receives HTTP 410
acceptance_checks.then: clean mappings outside that exact account/calendar SHALL remain unchanged

acceptance_checks.given: a new or unpublished Jin event and an enabled writable destination
acceptance_checks.then: one outbox operation SHALL reference that exact account/calendar target

acceptance_checks.given: Local only is selected
acceptance_checks.then: no provider outbox operation SHALL be created

acceptance_checks.given: any synced event is created, edited, or deleted through CLI or Tauri
acceptance_checks.then: exactly one recoverable destination-scoped outbox intent SHALL exist

acceptance_checks.given: a process stops between canonical write and outbox finalization
acceptance_checks.then: the canonical revision and its outbox intent SHALL converge idempotently

acceptance_checks.given: a non-cancelled Google event on an enabled available writer/owner calendar
acceptance_checks.then: core capability projection SHALL report it editable

acceptance_checks.given: an eligible Google-origin event
acceptance_checks.when: supported fields are edited in Jin
acceptance_checks.then: its sparse PATCH intent SHALL preserve target, remote identity, and base etag

acceptance_checks.given: an eligible Google-origin event
acceptance_checks.then: Google SHALL receive the delete on the event's persisted destination

acceptance_checks.given: a recurring Google event
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL preserve exception and original-start identity through round-trip

acceptance_checks.given: a recurring Google event
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL preserve master recurrence lines, timezone, and all-day end semantics

acceptance_checks.given: a recurring event mutation requests `This and following`
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL reject it without canonical or outbox mutation

acceptance_checks.given: Google returns 412 for a pending Google-origin edit
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL retain the remote representation without unconditional overwrite

acceptance_checks.given: a local Google-origin edit loses conflict resolution
acceptance_checks.then: the losing delta SHALL be appended under the same immutable account/calendar identity

acceptance_checks.given: a Jin-origin published event
acceptance_checks.when: its Google replica is deleted remotely
acceptance_checks.then: the Jin canonical event SHALL remain locally present as unpublished

acceptance_checks.given: one destination fails while another succeeds
acceptance_checks.then: the successful destination SHALL commit with both scoped outcomes reported

acceptance_checks.given: a disconnected account has paused outbox work
acceptance_checks.when: that same account is reauthenticated with sufficient role
acceptance_checks.then: only its original destinations SHALL resume after capability refresh

acceptance_checks.given: Jin and enabled Google events intersect the selected range
acceptance_checks.when: the selected Month, Week, or Day is projected
acceptance_checks.then: Month, Week, and Day SHALL project both source classes in one agenda

acceptance_checks.given: a provider-backed event crosses Rust, Tauri, and TypeScript boundaries
acceptance_checks.when: its DTO is serialized and decoded
acceptance_checks.then: its DTO SHALL preserve stable identity, display provenance, access role, and sync state
acceptance_checks.verify_method: test: Rust serialization fixture equals TypeScript fixture

acceptance_checks.given: multiple writable destinations exist without an explicit preference
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL return typed ambiguity instead of selecting a cross-account fallback

acceptance_checks.given: multiple accounts are configured
acceptance_checks.then: Settings SHALL render independently operable account cards with calendar toggles

acceptance_checks.given: any provider event mutation is ready to synchronize
acceptance_checks.then: Google payloads SHALL omit account aliases and every Jin-local context field

acceptance_checks.given: an account with cached events and audit records
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL retain those local records while pausing only that account's network work

acceptance_checks.given: no two-account live sandbox result has been recorded
acceptance_checks.then: release evidence SHALL label Google end-to-end behavior `live-unvalidated`
acceptance_checks.verify_method: review: docs/google-smoke-test.md result record and release checklist

acceptance_checks.given: initial OAuth succeeds for a newly generated Jin account ID
acceptance_checks.when: the account registry activates the connection
acceptance_checks.then: the account SHALL be immutably bound to Google's validated issuer and subject

acceptance_checks.given: a configured account is bound to one Google issuer and subject
acceptance_checks.when: reauthentication returns a different issuer or subject
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL reject the credentials without changing the stored token namespace

acceptance_checks.given: migration is interrupted after any v1-to-v2 phase
acceptance_checks.when: startup recovery reruns the same migration operation
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL converge to one complete v2 state or the intact v1 snapshot

acceptance_checks.given: a root carries the v2 account-registry activation marker
acceptance_checks.when: the current compatibility guard and frozen historical writer behavior are evaluated
acceptance_checks.then: current Jin SHALL reject legacy singleton operations before mutation, and lifecycle evidence SHALL record that an already-built historical binary is outside current-code enforcement
acceptance_checks.verify_method: test: config_migration_old_binary_write_guard_fixture; evidence: VIGIL pinned-historical-binary counterexample; review: planner-amendment-ac-gcal-043.md

acceptance_checks.given: v2 account credentials are active
acceptance_checks.when: token load, save, refresh, or delete cannot find the requested account namespace
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL fail without probing the legacy singleton credential slot

acceptance_checks.given: concurrent refresh requests target one account
acceptance_checks.then: an account-scoped lock and auth generation SHALL prevent an older refresh overwriting a newer token

acceptance_checks.given: two providers or accounts reuse calendar, event, and recurrence identifiers
acceptance_checks.when: mappings and outbox rows are persisted
acceptance_checks.then: schema constraints SHALL distinguish the complete provider/account/calendar/event/recurrence key

acceptance_checks.given: a calendar is inbound-enabled with reader-only provider access
acceptance_checks.when: pull and outbound capabilities are evaluated
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL allow inbound mirroring without authorizing outbound mutation

acceptance_checks.given: queued writes exist when provider role is downgraded or revoked
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL quarantine the writes until explicit review without automatic replay

acceptance_checks.given: an event mutation is accepted for one destination
acceptance_checks.when: its outbox operation is drained later
acceptance_checks.then: sync SHALL use the exact intent-time destination without alias, default, or primary fallback

acceptance_checks.given: Google returns 412 for a pending operation
acceptance_checks.when: the conflict audit record is appended
acceptance_checks.then: it SHALL contain scoped identity, operation, etags, redacted local delta, remote snapshot, policy, and winner

acceptance_checks.given: an account has cursors and pending outbox operations
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL clear only its cursors and quarantine only its pending operations

acceptance_checks.given: a disconnected account reconnects with the matching subject
acceptance_checks.then: no quarantined operation SHALL resume until the user explicitly reviews it

acceptance_checks.given: the user disconnects or hides a Google account
acceptance_checks.when: local cached data is considered for deletion
acceptance_checks.then: Jin SHALL require a separate destructive-removal operation not provided by disconnect

acceptance_checks.given: a queued write predates revocation, downgrade, disconnect, remote cancellation, or local tombstone
acceptance_checks.then: the newer safety generation SHALL quarantine or supersede it before any provider request
